References / Poster / 293

Pacific Wave, Museo Fortuny poster

April Greiman’s poster for an exhibition of California graphic design in Venice: a stippled wave photograph, pink and black fields with irregular white holes, and tilted bitmap type.

Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

The V&A holds the poster as E.1499-2010, colour offset lithograph, 98.5 × 68 cm, and describes it as a poster for “Pacific Wave”, an exhibition of California graphic design at the Museo Fortuny, Venice, September 1987. V&A E.1499-2010.

Observed

  • A yellow bar runs across the top and down the right side, fading through red to blue.
  • Large black and hot-pink fields fill the sheet. Irregular white shapes with soft, blob-like edges cut holes through them.
  • A photograph of a breaking wave is rendered in coarse white stipple over a yellow-red-blue gradient panel.
  • “pacific wave” runs on a rising diagonal in white bitmap letters with broken, ragged edges, followed by dotted lines. A second, smaller copy sits on the pink field.
  • Small text runs vertically in narrow black and pink strips at the left.

Why it belongs

This is the style at its most digital. The ragged bitmap letters come near the grunge counter-rule, but they are low-resolution output, not deliberate damage. Treat it as the edge of the style, not a model for it.

Borrow

Run a gradient bar around two edges of a composition as a frame.

Set a title on a steep diagonal and repeat it smaller in another layer.
